ai.description: This small toad reaches 35–40 mm. It is brown with a dark, triangular dorsal mark and a distinct, pointed snout projection. Its skin is granular with prominent dorsolateral folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys oropedion* is best distinguished by its uniquely small body size and the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like projection on each upper eyelid.
ai.habitat: The Shyllong Horned Toad inhabits high-altitude evergreen broadleaf forests and moist rocky streams in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Shyllong Horned Toad is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter during the day to ambush small invertebrate prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: The *Megophrys oropedion* breeds in streams during the monsoon season. It lays small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys oropedion* is endemic to the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Shillong horned toad emits a sharp, high-pitched "tink" or "click" sound, typically heard as a single, isolated note from the leaf litter of moist forest floors.
